title: Who shoots
summary: Clay shooting is open to all ages: juniors, women, veterans and whole families shoot together. Here is how categories work and how to find company at a club.

body.html: Clay shooting is one of the few sports where a teenager, a parent and a grandparent can shoot side by side on the same field. Accuracy, attention and self-control count for more than strength or height.

To keep competitions fair, results are also ranked in categories. Besides the open ranking for everyone, there are age and gender categories. At international FITASC competitions from 1 January 2027 they are: Junior (13–20), Lady (from 13), Men (21–55), Senior (56–65), Veteran (66–72) and Master (from 73), counted by year of birth, not by birthday. National and club events may use their own categories, so check the programme before you enter. More on categories and shoot-offs (extra targets to break a tie): Categories, classes and shoot-offs.

Children start only under the supervision of adults and a coach. The minimum age and the rules for minors depend on national law and on the ground's own rules. Young shooters often get a lighter gun with a narrower barrel (a 20 gauge instead of the usual 12). It is used with light cartridges: the light cartridge is what makes the recoil (the kick into the shoulder) softer, because with the same cartridge a lighter gun kicks harder. More: When a child can start.

At competitions people shoot in squads: small groups put together by a draw. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™, and in Compak® Sporting when it is shot by squad, a squad has at most six shooters. You may end up next to a champion, which is a good chance to learn just by watching.
Many people shoot for relaxation and company and do not compete at all. A shooting ground is also a place to meet people, share experience and spend weekends as a family.

Many clubs run ladies' days and women's training groups. There you can try shooting in a relaxed setting, borrow a gun and talk to experienced women shooters. Some clubs also have women coaches. Ask at your club.

For inspiration, look at the results of the Lady category at world and continental championships; some women also finish high in the open ranking. Results, videos and shooter profiles are on ClayArena.

html: Book a taster session with a coach at a ground.
Shoot the ground's gun with light cartridges.
Bring safety glasses and hearing protection, or borrow them at the ground.
After a few sessions, have a gun fitting (the stock is adjusted to your body); only then think about a gun of your own.
Ask the ground which gun and cartridge rules apply in your country.

key_points.html: Age, gender and strength matter less than attention and practice.
There is an open ranking plus categories; FITASC from 2027: Junior, Lady, Men, Senior, Veteran, Master. National and club events may have their own categories: see the programme.
Children shoot only under supervision; laws differ between countries.
At competitions you shoot in a squad of at most six shooters, put together by a draw.
Look for ladies' days and women's groups at clubs.

did_you_know.html: It is not unusual for several generations of one family to shoot at the same competition.

quiz.q: Who decides which categories apply at a competition?

options.text: FITASC at international events, else the programme
Each shooter chooses one when entering
The referee decides on the day

quiz.explain: International events use the FITASC category table (the new one from 1 January 2027); national and club events may have their own, and the programme states them.

quiz.q: What is the largest number of shooters in one squad?
quiz.explain: In Sporting™, and in Compak® Sporting when it is shot by squad, a squad has at most six shooters.

quiz.q: What should you remember about children at a ground?

options.text: They may shoot alone once trained

quiz.explain: Children shoot only with adults and a coach; the minimum age is set by law and by the ground's rules.
